config.classes_note: Three classes: (1) web archives and the readback of a page by URL and date (field B2, B6; census question and tll_reading); (2) digital libraries, book digitization and lending (field B1, B2; census kind, record_type, evidence_kind); (3) web crawls and corpora whose texts enter machine training (field B2's crawlers and its scraping sentence, B10's Common Crawl against the Wayback Machine; census area 'corpora', evidence_kind 'web crawl', record.in_layer). The aliases are the entity's name, its web archive, its library catalogue project and its host (the bare host only, not archived-copy URLs, which are citation apparatus: a link to web.archive.org is a use of the service and no claim about it). Brewster Kahle (its founder), Common Crawl, HathiTrust and Project Gutenberg (neighbours with rows of their own in the census), arXiv and archive.today (Wikipedia's disambiguation) are distinct entities and are not aliases. The census's tll_reading applies #186's and #1543's question (how transmission, transformation and provenance can be inspected across later reception) to the entity: that reading is the archive's, ledgered as TLL-NN. #186 and #1543, the census's anchors, are read at the passages that bear on training corpora, crawls and digital libraries, persistence and inspection. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the entity and says something of it; R where it states a relation between the entity and an archive object; O-class where a sentence applies an archive category to one of the three classes; a bare mention, an archived-copy link or a citation line is not a claim.
